questions.question: Which signal primarily provides high surface topography contrast in SEM imaging?
What is the primary purpose of sputter coating non-conductive samples before SEM?

answers.b: To increase electrical conductivity and reduce charging
answers.d: To improve chemical composition analysis by EDS

questions.question: In SEM, an increase in accelerating voltage typically results in:

answers.a: Reduced penetration depth and shallower interaction volume
answers.b: Larger interaction volume and deeper specimen penetration

questions.question: Which factor improves depth of field in SEM images?

answers.a: Low working distance and high accelerating voltage
answers.b: High condenser aperture and low magnification
answers.c: Large depth of field is intrinsic and cannot be changed
answers.d: Long working distance and small aperture (low probe size)

questions.question: What is "charging" in SEM and how is it minimized?

answers.a: Charging is detector overload and is minimized by turning off detectors
answers.b: Charging is electron accumulation on insulating samples, minimized by conductive coating or low vacuum
answers.c: Charging is caused by too much staining and fixed by washing
answers.d: Charging is sample electrification due to ions and is minimized by helium gas

questions.question: Which EM technique allows 3D reconstruction of cellular volumes via serial sectioning or tomography?

answers.b: Electron tomography or serial block-face SEM

questions.question: Which gas is often used in variable-pressure SEM modes to reduce charging on non-conductive samples?
Which coating material is commonly used to improve conductivity for SEM imaging of biological samples?
Which approach helps reduce charging and beam damage when imaging polymers or biological specimens in SEM?

answers.a: Use of highest possible accelerating voltage
answers.b: Coating with conductive film and using low accelerating voltage or low vacuum
answers.c: Immersing the sample in water during imaging
answers.d: Using visible light to pre-irradiate the sample
